name: Cataract(s)

category.name: Eye
category.part: AME Physical Examination Information and Disposition Tables

what_to_bring: A current, detailed Clinical Progress Note generated from a clinic visit with the treating ophthalmologist or optometrist no more than 90 days prior to the AME exam. It must include:
A detailed summary of the history of the condition;
Current medications, dosage, and side effects (if any);

The Clinical Progress note must specifically include the best corrected visual acuity for distant and near vision (intermediate - if age 50 or older and first or second Class). If vision standards are not met, that should be discussed. Include if the visual acuity is expected to change.
Copies of any testing performed (visual fields, etc.)

rows.label: A
rows.condition: Cataract(s) present; The individual meets the vision standards for class applied; and quality of vision is not affected: For more information see Pilot Vision
rows.condition_html:
A.

Cataract(s) present;

The individual meets the vision standards for class applied; and

quality of vision is not affected:

For more information see Pilot Vision
rows.evaluation_data: If the AME can determine the condition is under control and vision meets standards with no symptoms that would interfere with flight or safety-related duties such as: - Glare - Halos - Loss of contrast sensitivity - Poor night vision
rows.evaluation_data_html:
If the AME can determine the condition is under control and vision meets standards with no symptoms that would interfere with flight or safety-related duties such as:

  • Glare
  • Halos
  • Loss of contrast sensitivity
  • Poor night vision
rows.disposition: ISSUE Annotate Block 60. If correction was needed to meet standards, apply Limitation 102 to certificate. Warn the pilot CFR 61.53 applies if any change or worsening in vision.
rows.disposition_html:
ISSUE

rows.label: B
rows.condition: Others: - Does not meet vision standards - Quality of vision is affected - AME or ophthalmologist or optometrist have concerns
rows.condition_html:
B. Others:

  • Does not meet vision standards
  • Quality of vision is affected
  • AME or ophthalmologist or optometrist have concerns

rows.evaluation_data_html:
Submit the following for FAA review:

  • 1. A current, detailed Clinical Progress Note generated from a clinic visit with the treating ophthalmologist or optometrist no more than 90 days prior to the AME exam. It must include:
  • A detailed summary of the history of the condition;
  • Current medications, dosage, and side effects (if any);
  • Physical exam findings;
  • Results of any testing performed;
  • Diagnosis;
  • Assessment and plan;
  • Prognosis; and Follow-up.

2. The Clinical Progress note must specifically include the best corrected visual acuity for distant and near vision (intermediate - if age 50 or older and first or second Class). If vision standards are not met, that should be discussed. Include if the visual acuity is expected to change.

3. Copies of any testing performed (visual fields, etc.)

4. Quality of Vision Questionnaire

rows.disposition: DEFER Submit the information to the FAA for a possible Special Issuance Annotate (elements or findings) in Block 60. Note: If unable to meet 1st or 2nd class visual acuity standards, but they will accept a lower class, the AME should issue 3rd class and annotate block 60.
